{{nihongo|'''Imoni'''|芋煮}} is a type of [[taro]] and [[meat]] soup eaten traditionally in the autumn in the [[Tōhoku region]] of Japan. [[Yamagata Prefecture]] in particular is famous for its imoni, but other prefectures in the region also have their own different varieties.

Imoni is eaten like any soup, primarily during the late summer and early autumn, but is most famous as an outdoor food. In the autumn, groups of people preparing imoni around a fire near a river is considered a sign of the season, and [[convenience store]]s maintain a stock of firewood and other supplies just for the occasion.
